## The problem in one synthetic cohort

`bulkmask` reports how much of a bulk RNA-seq association between two genes is
shared with an estimated cell compartment. It does not test per-cell regulation,
which requires cell-resolved data. This vignette needs no external data: we simulate a cohort
in which a rare effector compartment (think eosinophils) drives a positive bulk
correlation between an exposure gene and an outcome gene, even though there is no
direct per-cell link.

```{r load}
# devtools::load_all("bulkmask")  # during development
library(bulkmask)
set.seed(42)

n        <- 400
compart  <- rnorm(n)                       # latent effector-cell abundance
exposure <- 0.9 * compart + rnorm(n, sd = 0.6)
outcome  <- 0.9 * compart + rnorm(n, sd = 0.6)   # no direct exposure->outcome link
group    <- as.integer(compart > 0)        # "disease" expands the compartment
```

## Step 3: composition-adjusted partial correlation

```{r partial}
raw <- partial_corr(exposure, outcome)                       # ordinary Spearman
adj <- partial_corr(exposure, outcome, list(eos = compart))  # condition on compartment
c(raw_rho = raw$rho, raw_p = raw$p)
c(adj_rho = adj$rho, adj_p = adj$p)
```

The positive raw association collapses once we condition on the compartment, as
expected here: the simulated association is carried entirely by the compartment.

## Step 4: bootstrap decomposition

```{r decompose}
d   <- data.frame(exposure, outcome, med = compart, group_bin = group)
dec <- decompose_association(d, "exposure", "med", "outcome", R = 500)
dec[, c("ACME", "ACME_p", "ADE", "ADE_p", "total_effect", "prop_mediated")]
```

`prop_mediated` near 1 with a residual (`ADE`) indistinguishable from zero means
the bulk association is almost entirely *composition-associated*. Add a nuisance
covariate (e.g. case/control status) with `covariates = "group_bin"`.

```{r decompose-adj}
decg <- decompose_association(d, "exposure", "med", "outcome",
                              covariates = "group_bin", R = 500)
decg[, c("ACME", "ADE", "prop_mediated", "covariates")]
```

## Applying it to your own data

Copy `inst/config/idi2as1_il5.yml`; set `exposure` and `exposure_ensembl`,
`outcome` and `outcome_ensembl`, the marker `signatures` with their
`ensembl_aliases`, `mediator_signature` and `deconvolution: xcell_cell_type` for
your compartment, and the `cohorts`. Then run steps 2–4 with `prepare_cohort()` +
`analyse_cohort()` (see `scripts/run_bulkmask_pipeline.R`); step 1 (`run_de()`)
is run separately. Count cohorts are length-normalised to TPM for the
deconvolution input. The mediator compartment is estimated three ways (marker
z-score, xCell raw enrichment, GSVA ssGSEA of the same markers). They are not
independent — two share the marker genes and xCell shares some of them — so
their agreement tests robustness to the summarization more than to the choice
of genes.

> All effects are reported as a **statistical partition under a linear model on
> cross-sectional data, not a causal effect.**
